subject.title: fix(models): add provider request rate limits

question: Should OpenClaw core accept this new opt-in `models.providers.*.request.rateLimit` provider-dispatch config as the first slice of outbound API governance?
rationale: The PR adds a public config/runtime contract and intentionally covers only model-provider HTTP dispatch, while the related canonical issue also asks for budgets, observability, CLI/status UX, backoff, tools, and channel/plugin calls.

options.title: Provider Dispatch First
options.body: Land the opt-in provider request limiter after rebase and proof, and keep broader budgets/status/tool/channel work in the canonical tracker.

options.title: Broader Design First
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers design the full outbound governance surface across providers, tools, channels, budgets, status, and alerts.

options.title: No Core Config Yet
options.body: Decline this config surface for now and ask for a plugin/API-seam proposal or narrower core primitive instead.

recommendation.title: Provider Dispatch First
recommendation.body: Land the opt-in provider request limiter after rebase and proof, and keep broader budgets/status/tool/channel work in the canonical tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest product-scoping signal on the related tracker and recent ownership of the provider egress boundary this PR must preserve.
